checkpoints.cue: Spinach is evenly distributed without puddles in the filling.
checkpoints.why: Squeezing free water limits leakage between layers; the spinach is not literally moisture-free.

checkpoints.cue: Noodles are tender through every tier and multiple centers reach 165°F / 74°C.
checkpoints.why: Bubbling edges alone do not show that the center or sheets have finished.

troubleshooting.cause: The covered hydration stage or product suitability was inadequate.
troubleshooting.fix: Re-cover and continue checking tenderness and center temperature; do not assume browning the top fixes dry sheets. Confirm the noodle package method before the next batch.

substitutions.alternative: For the saved seasoning option, replace the main listed kosher salt with ¼ tsp unnamed salt for the original batch, scaled proportionally, and omit the main pepper. Keep all cheese, spinach, egg, sauce and pasta amounts and the same layer proportions and center checks. The source rests 5 minutes; the main 10-minute rest remains available for firmer slicing.
substitutions.effect: This is a distinct source volume, not a conversion between unnamed salt and kosher crystals.

substitutions.alternative: Assemble, cover and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below, then cook within 24 hours. Use a vessel whose manufacturer permits the intended refrigerator-to-oven transition. Keep the same oven setting and check noodles and centers; do not assume exactly 10 extra minutes.
substitutions.effect: This retains the current one-day preparation plan without certifying a cold glass dish or a universal added clock.

after.storage: Refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C, at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use within 3–4 days and reheat throughout to 165°F / 74°C. Thaw frozen portions in the refrigerator. For an assembled raw-egg dish, refrigerate and cook within 24 hours; use the vessel maker’s transition instructions.
after.timing: About 75–80 minutes includes 15 minutes assembly, 50–55 minutes baking and 10 minutes rest for the original pan. Thawing/required spinach preparation, preheat still pending, chilled assembly and other pan loads can add time.

exactBodyChange.before:
## Chef's Note

Lasagna originated in Naples and is one of Italy's oldest pasta dishes, with recipes dating back to the 14th century. The no-boil lasagna sheets are a modern American invention from the 1990s that saves time but requires a saucier sauce to hydrate properly during baking. Squeeze that spinach bone-dry - frozen spinach holds an astonishing amount of water that will make your lasagna watery. This is perfect make-ahead food: assemble up to 24 hours in advance, refrigerate covered, and add 10 minutes to baking time.

## Directions

1.  **The Filling:** In a large bowl, whisk the egg. Mix in the ricotta, mozzarella, 3/4 cup of the Parmesan, the squeezed spinach, salt, and pepper until well combined.
2.  **Layer 1:** Spread 3/4 cup of sauce on the bottom of a 9x13 inch baking dish. This prevents the bottom noodles from sticking.
3.  **Layer 2:** Place a layer of no-boil noodles on top (they shouldn't overlap much). Spread 1/3 of the cheese mixture over the noodles, then top with another 3/4 cup of sauce.
4.  **Repeat:** Repeat the layers (Noodles -> Cheese -> Sauce) until all ingredients are used, ending with a final layer of sauce.
5.  **Finish:** Top with the remaining 1/4 cup Parmesan. Cover tightly with foil.
6.  **Bake:** Bake at 375°F for 30 minutes.
7.  **Crisp:** Remove the foil and bake for another 20-25 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and the noodles are tender.
8.  **Rest:** Let the lasagna rest for 10 minutes before slicing. This is critical for the layers to set.
exactBodyChange.after:
## Chef's Note

Squeeze the thawed spinach until free water stops dripping, then distribute it throughout the cheese mixture. Divide the sauce before layering so the bottom and all three noodle tiers receive their share. No-boil sheets hydrate inside the covered dish; use a product suitable for this sauce-and-bake method and check every layer for tenderness.

## Directions

1. **Mix:** Preheat the oven to 375°F. Thaw the spinach under refrigeration, follow any required product preparation, and squeeze out free liquid; cool any cooked spinach before mixing it with egg. Combine ricotta cheese, mozzarella cheese, 3/4 of the Parmesan cheese, frozen spinach, large egg, kosher salt, and black pepper in a large bowl: whisk the egg first, then fold in the cheeses, prepared spinach and seasonings until the cheese and spinach are evenly distributed.
2. **Base:** Spread 1/4 of the marinara sauce over the bottom of a 9×13-inch baking dish for the original batch. At other scales use enough separate original-size dishes or an appropriately smaller dish with similar layer depth and headroom; do not force the scaled mixture into the same pan.
3. **First tier:** Build the first tier with 1/4 of the marinara sauce and 1/3 of the whole-wheat no-boil lasagna sheets: arrange the noodle portion over the base without excessive overlap, spread one third of the full cheese mixture over the noodles, then add this sauce portion.
4. **Remaining tiers:** Build two more tiers with 1/2 of the marinara sauce and 2/3 of the whole-wheat no-boil lasagna sheets and the remaining cheese mixture, dividing each of those supplies into two equal portions. In each tier arrange noodles, then cheese mixture, then sauce. Use all the remaining sauce, ending with sauce on top; do not add an extra noodle layer.
5. **Cover:** Scatter 1/4 of the Parmesan cheese over the final sauce. Cover the dish tightly with foil.
6. **Bake covered:** Bake at 375°F for about 30 minutes for the original pan.
7. **Finish uncovered:** Remove foil and continue baking, checking after about 20–25 minutes, until bubbling, the sheets are tender through all layers and several center locations reach 165°F / 74°C. A chilled or differently loaded dish can take longer.
8. **Rest:** Rest 10 minutes before cutting and serving.
